expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: { status: 'canceled'; cancellation: Cancellation } — each arm lists only its own fields; no shared optionals

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never): never { ... }  and  default: return assertNever(sub); // Compile error if a status is missing

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type Brand<T, B> = T & { readonly [brand]: B }; export type SubscriptionId = Brand<string, "SubscriptionId">;

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function is provided; it is explicitly listed under 'What I consciously left possible' — 'nothing prevents going from canceled back to trialing... If that matters, add a transition function' and offered as a follow-up question

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Table: '"trialing with a cancel_reason" and 60 other nonsense states | Discriminated union — only 4 states are representable'; also '"voluntary: true, reason: payment-failed"' listed with its device

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "The subscription itself - discriminated union, not bag of optionals" — optionals are only described as the hazard to avoid
